mainTopic: Cutting spice wood and toothpicks on שבת and יום טוב, and lines of the משנה about gathering fuel, making fire and heating tiles
overview: The amud opens with רב יהודה's rule that animal fodder carries no problem of תיקון כלי. רב כהנא challenges him from a בריתא about spice wood. The גמרא explains that the בריתא is missing words and is really teaching two cases: soft wood may be cut to smell it, but hard wood may not. רב אחא בר יעקב objects that cutting hard wood should be no worse than breaking a חבית to get figs, and adds that רב יהודה himself broke off hard spice sticks. The גמרא answers that this depends on a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים about breaking off a toothpick. Cutting wood just to smell it is one level more lenient than cutting a toothpick under each opinion. רב אשי then explains that the חבית משנה is about a barrel that was already patched, so it fits רבי אליעזר too. The גמרא then explains three more lines of the משנה: gathering fuel from the courtyard, why one may not make new fire on יום טוב, and the ban on heating new tiles, whose reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Animal fodder has no problem of making a utensil
steps.stepSummary: The rule is stated: cutting animal fodder does not count as making a utensil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Animal food does not carry the problem of making a utensil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a simple rule: things that are animal food are not treated as utensils, so trimming them is not 'making a utensil.' This is the rule that רב כהנא is about to challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making something into a usable tool is a forbidden מלאכה, called תיקון כלי. Since straw and similar fodder are seen as food, shaping a piece of it is not considered making a utensil. The next step attacks this rule from a בריתא.

keyTerms.meaning: making or fixing a utensil, a forbidden act

phrases.english: Animal fodder
does not have a problem of preparing a utensil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹכְלֵי בְּהֵמָה אֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם תִּקּוּן כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by stating the principle behind רב יהודה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting or shaping animal fodder is not considered תיקון כלי.

steps.title: רב כהנא's challenge from the spice-wood בריתא
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא quotes a בריתא that forbids cutting spice wood and even makes one חייב חטאת for cutting it to clean teeth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא challenged רב יהודה: A בריתא says one may move spice wood to smell it or to fan a sick person, and may crush it and smell it. But one may not cut it to smell it, and if he did, he is exempt but it is forbidden. To clean his teeth with it, he may not cut it, and if he did, he must bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא brings a בריתא that seems to contradict רב יהודה. The בריתא treats cutting spice wood for a toothpick as a real violation of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fodder never carries a problem of making a utensil, cutting a twig to clean one's teeth should be fine. Yet the בריתא says this cutting makes a person חייב חטאת, the strongest level of guilt. The challenge assumes that this spice wood is the kind of thing animals eat.

keyTerms.meaning: he crushes it between his fingers
he will cut or snap it off
must bring a sin offering, a full Torah violation

phrases.english: Rav Kahana challenged Rav Yehuda:
One may move spice wood to smell it,
and to wave it in front of a sick person,
and he may crush it and smell it.
But he may not cut it off to smell it,
and if he cut it, he is exempt but it is forbidden.
To clean his teeth with it, he may not cut it,
and if he cut it, he must bring a sin offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule of step 1 from a בריתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that animal fodder carries no problem of תיקון כלי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בריתא makes cutting spice wood for a toothpick a full חטאת violation, which treats it as making a utensil.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the בריתא is about hard wood
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says he cannot read the בריתא as being about fodder at all, so it must be speaking about hard wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even 'exempt but forbidden' is hard for me to accept. Do you need to ask about 'he must bring a חטאת'? Rather, that בריתא was taught about hard wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that the בריתא cannot be about soft, fodder-like wood. It must be talking about hard wood, which is not animal food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה turns the challenge around. In his view, if the wood were fodder, even a mild 'forbidden' would not fit, let alone a חטאת. So the בריתא must be speaking about hard pieces of wood, which are not food, and there the problem of making a utensil does apply.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר
phrases.english: He said to him: Now, 'exempt but forbidden'
is already difficult for me,
phrases.notes: He means that if this were fodder, he would allow cutting it completely.

phrases.english: so do I even need to ask about 'he must bring a sin offering'?
Rather, that בריתא was taught about hard wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הַשְׁתָּא פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר קָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by limiting the בריתא to a different case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the בריתא speaks of hard wood, which is not fodder.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בריתא is about ordinary spice wood that counts as animal fodder.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בריתא is about hard wood, so it does not contradict the fodder rule.

steps.title: Can hard wood be crushed by hand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's answer: the בריתא says the wood may be crushed, and hard wood cannot be crushed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can hard wood be crushed by hand?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יהודה's answer. The same בריתא says 'he crushes it and smells it,' and that does not fit hard wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בריתא is one continuous teaching about the same wood. If it is all about hard wood, the line 'he may crush it' makes no sense, because hard branches cannot be crushed between the fingers. So the answer that 'the whole בריתא is about hard wood' seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: crushing by rubbing between the fingers

phrases.english: Are hard pieces of wood able to be crushed?
phrases.notes: This refers back to 'he crushes it and smells it' in the בריתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָשִׁין בְּנֵי מְלִילָה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that the בריתא is about hard wood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בריתא allows crushing the wood by hand, which only works for soft wood.

steps.title: The בריתא is missing words: soft wood versus hard wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the בריתא with missing words added. Soft wood may be crushed and cut. Hard wood may not be cut: for smell it is exempt but forbidden, and for a toothpick it is a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Words are missing, and this is what the בריתא teaches: He may crush it and smell it, and cut it and smell it. When is this said? With soft wood. But with hard wood, he may not cut it, and if he cut it he is exempt but it is forbidden. To clean his teeth with it, he may not cut it, and if he cut it, he must bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the בריתא by adding missing words. Now the בריתא speaks about two kinds of wood, soft and hard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the בריתא, crushing and even cutting, is about soft wood, which is like fodder. That fits רב יהודה's rule. The strict parts, 'exempt but forbidden' and the חטאת, are about hard wood only. So the בריתא no longer contradicts רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: words are missing from the text
and this is what it teaches
in what case was this said?

steps.whatToRemember: Soft wood, which is like animal fodder, may be crushed and even cut. Hard wood may not be cut. Cutting it to smell is exempt but forbidden, and cutting it to clean one's teeth is a full חטאת. This saves רב יהודה's rule.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'missing words' do not mean the בריתא is wrong. The גמרא is showing that it was teaching two cases, soft and hard, and a few words that make this clear were left out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic חסורי מחסרא move. Adding the missing words splits one teaching into two cases, and the contradiction disappears.

phrases.english: Words are missing, and this is what it teaches:
He may crush it and smell it,
and cut it and smell it.
In what case is this said? With soft wood,
but with hard wood, he may not cut it,
and if he cut it, he is exempt but it is forbidden.
To clean his teeth with it, he may not cut it,
and if he cut it, he must bring a sin offering.
phrases.notes: This last part is about hard wood too, which is not fodder.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַסּוֹרֵי מְחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by rereading the בריתא as covering both soft and hard wood.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מחסרא: missing words are added to the בריתא, splitting it into two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole בריתא speaks about one kind of wood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient parts are about soft wood and the strict parts are about hard wood, so רב יהודה's rule stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Soft, fodder-like wood may be crushed and cut. Hard wood may not be cut: for smell it is exempt but forbidden, and for a toothpick it is a חטאת.

steps.title: Two teachings contradict each other about cutting spice wood to smell it
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא allows cutting a stick of spice wood to smell it. Another ברייתא forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: he may cut it and smell it. Another ברייתא teaches: he may not cut it in order to smell it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two ברייתות side by side that seem to say opposite things about cutting spice wood to smell it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות speak about the same act: breaking off a piece of fragrant wood to enjoy its smell. One says it is allowed and one says it is not, so we need a way to tell them apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He breaks it off or cuts it

phrases.english: One ברייתא teaches:
He may cut it and smell it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the stick of spice wood from the ברייתא the גמרא was just discussing.

phrases.english: Another ברייתא teaches:
He may not cut it in order to smell it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא קוֹטְמוֹ וּמֵרִיחַ בּוֹ תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ לֹא יִקְטְמֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the soft wood and hard wood split from step 5 by bringing a second pair of sources that conflict about smelling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about cutting spice wood to smell it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same act is called both allowed and forbidden, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: Soft wood may be cut, hard wood may not
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא settles the contradiction. The ברייתא that allows it is about soft wood, and the one that forbids it is about hard wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב חסדא: It is not difficult. This one is about soft wood, and that one is about hard wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soft wood is not useful for building anything, so cutting it is like cutting food. Hard wood could be made into a tool, so cutting it looks more like making a כלי. That is why the hard wood case is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources can be reconciled

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Chisda said:
It is not difficult:
This one, which permits, is about soft wood,
that one, which forbids, is about hard wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא בְּרַכִּין הָא בְּקָשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is about a different type of wood
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be about the same wood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permitting ברייתא is about soft wood, and the forbidding one is about hard wood.

steps.title: Why should hard wood be any worse than breaking a barrel?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב asks why cutting hard wood is forbidden, since a משנה allows breaking a חבית to get at the figs inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב objected: With hard wood, why not? How is it different from what we learned in a משנה: A person may break a barrel to eat dried figs from it, as long as he does not intend to make a utensil!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב attacks רב חסדא's answer by asking why cutting hard wood should be forbidden at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חבית is a real, finished כלי, and the משנה still lets you break it to reach your food, as long as you are not trying to make a new כלי. Breaking a stick of hard wood just to smell it seems no worse, so it should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: As long as he does not intend

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov objected to this:
With hard wood, why not?
How is it different from what we learned in a משנה:
A person may break the barrel
in order to eat dried figs from it,
as long as he does not intend to make a utensil!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב בְּקָשִׁין אַמַּאי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 7 that hard wood may not be cut.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that cutting hard wood to smell it is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If breaking a real כלי to get food is allowed, then breaking hard wood to smell it should be allowed too.

steps.title: רב יהודה himself broke off hard spice sticks
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: רב יהודה used to break off sticks of spice wood hard enough for ax handles and hand them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: רבא בר רב אדא and רבין בר רב אדא both said: When we were at רב יהודה's house, he would break off and give us stick after stick of spice wood, even though they were fit for handles of axes and hatchets.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge continues with a story: רב יהודה, a great authority, broke off hard spice sticks for his students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sticks strong enough for ax handles are clearly hard wood. If רב יהודה broke them off, then cutting hard wood to smell it must be allowed, which goes against רב חסדא.

phrases.english: And furthermore:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רָבָא בַּר רַב אַדָּא וְרָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא
phrases.english: there are Rava bar Rav Adda and Ravin bar Rav Adda
who both said:
When we were at Rav Yehuda's house,
he would break off and give us
stick after stick of spice wood,
even though they were fit
for handles of axes and hatchets.
phrases.notes: In other words, this was hard wood, the very kind רב חסדא said may not be cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד הָא רָבָא בַּר רַב אַדָּא וְרָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the same ruling attacked in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that cutting hard wood is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה actually broke off hard wood, which shows it is allowed.

steps.title: It depends on a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the forbidding view follows רבי אליעזר, while the חבית case and רב יהודה's practice follow the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this follows רבי אליעזר, and that follows the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenges by saying the sources follow two different opinions. It is setting up the ברייתא that shows this מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not deny either source. It says the rule that hard wood is forbidden belongs to רבי אליעזר, and the more lenient sources belong to the חכמים. The next steps show where this מחלוקת comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, the majority of the תנאים, who are more lenient

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this follows Rabbi Eliezer, and that follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: "This," the ban on hard wood, is רבי אליעזר. "That," the lenient sources, is the חכמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two challenges from steps 8 and 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees on one rule, so the sources clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict view is רבי אליעזר's, and the lenient sources follow the חכמים.

steps.title: The ברייתא about toothpicks: רבי אליעזר's strict view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the מחלוקת about taking a toothpick, and רבי אליעזר's view that breaking one off is a real מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says a person may take a sliver of wood from what is in front of him to pick his teeth. The חכמים say he may take one only from an animal's trough. They agree that he may not break one off. If he broke it off to pick his teeth or to open a door with it, then by mistake on שבת he must bring a חטאת, and on purpose on יום טוב he gets forty lashes. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows the מחלוקת. Here we see רבי אליעזר's strict opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that you may not break off a sliver of wood. For רבי אליעזר, doing so to make a toothpick or a door key is a real מלאכה from the תורה: a חטאת on שבת, or lashes on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A sliver of wood, a toothpick
To pick or clean his teeth

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A person may take a sliver of wood from what is in front of him
to pick his teeth with it,
and the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִטּוֹל אֶלָּא מֵאֵבוּס שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.english: He may take one only from an animal's trough.
And they agree that he may not break it off,
and if he broke it off to pick his teeth with it
or to open the door with it,
if by mistake on Shabbos, he must bring a sin-offering;

phrases.aramaic: בְּמֵזִיד בְּיוֹם טוֹב — סוֹפֵג אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים,
phrases.english: if on purpose on Yom Tov, he receives the forty lashes.
These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר נוֹטֵל אָדָם קֵיסָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the מחלוקת named in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and the חכמים disagree about breaking off wood
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about taking or breaking off a toothpick on שבת and יום טוב

steps.title: The חכמים: breaking off a toothpick is only a rabbinic ban
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that on both שבת and יום טוב, breaking off the sliver is only a שבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: Both in this case and in that case, it is forbidden only because of a rabbinic rest rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the חכמים, who disagree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, breaking off a sliver of wood is not a real מלאכה from the תורה at all, even to make a toothpick or a key. It is forbidden only מדרבנן, so there is no חטאת and no lashes.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
both in this case and in that case,
phrases.notes: Both שבת and יום טוב, whether he wanted a toothpick or a key.

phrases.english: it is forbidden only because of a rabbinic rest rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from step 11 with the חכמים's opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaking off a sliver of wood is only a שבות, forbidden מדרבנן, not a מלאכה from the תורה.

steps.title: Applying the מחלוקת to cutting wood for smelling
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אליעזר, cutting hard wood to smell it is פטור אבל אסור. For the חכמים, it is מותר לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says there, about a toothpick, that he must bring a חטאת. So here, cutting wood to smell it is exempt but forbidden. The Rabbis say there that it is exempt but forbidden. So here, it is permitted from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves each opinion down one level to fit our case of cutting wood just to smell it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smelling is a weaker purpose than making a toothpick, because no tool is being made. So רבי אליעזר's חטאת becomes פטור אבל אסור, which is the ban on hard wood. The חכמים's פטור אבל אסור becomes fully allowed, which explains the חבית case and רב יהודה's practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from punishment, but still forbidden
There, in the toothpick case / here, in the smelling case

steps.whatToRemember: Cutting wood to smell it is always one level more lenient than cutting a toothpick. For רבי אליעזר it is פטור אבל אסור, which is why hard wood is forbidden. For the חכמים it is fully allowed, as רב יהודה did.
steps.confusionAlert: "Exempt" for רבי אליעזר does not mean allowed. It means there is no חטאת, but you still may not do it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, who says there,
that he must bring a sin-offering,
here holds it is exempt but forbidden.
phrases.notes: "Here" is cutting spice wood just to smell it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis, who say there
that it is exempt but forbidden,
here hold it is permitted from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּקָאָמַר הָתָם חַיָּיב חַטָּאת הָכָא פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from steps 11 and 12 to the smelling case, finishing the answer begun in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ban on cutting hard wood to smell it follows רבי אליעזר (פטור אבל אסור). The חכמים allow it לכתחילה, which matches the חבית משנה and רב יהודה's practice.

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר reject the barrel-breaking משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's strict view from a משנה that lets a person break a barrel to eat figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אליעזר not accept the משנה that says a person may break a barrel to eat dried figs from it, as long as he does not mean to make a vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר. A משנה lets a person break a barrel to get food, as long as he is not trying to make a כלי. So how can רבי אליעזר say that cutting wood just to smell it is still forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 we learned that for רבי אליעזר, breaking hard wood is פטור אבל אסור. Yet the חבית משנה seems to allow breaking a whole vessel from the start. Breaking a whole barrel seems like a bigger deal than snapping off a twig, so the משנה looks like it argues with רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he not hold of this?

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Eliezer not hold
this that we learned in a Mishnah:
A person may break the barrel
to eat dried figs from it,
provided that he does not intend to make a vessel?
phrases.notes: So breaking it is allowed from the start, which sounds more lenient than רבי אליעזר's 'פטור אבל אסור.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבי אליעזר position stated in the conclusion of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view (step 13) that cutting wood just to smell it is פטור אבל אסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה lets a person break a whole barrel to get food. That seems to contradict רבי אליעזר's stricter view about breaking wood.

steps.title: רב אשי: the barrel was already patched
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the barrel משנה is about a barrel that had already been broken and glued together with pitch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That teaching is about a מוסתקי, a barrel that was patched with pitch.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends רבי אליעזר. He explains that the משנה is talking about a barrel that was already broken before and patched up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A patched barrel is not a fully whole vessel. Breaking it apart again is not like smashing a complete כלי. So the משנה's leniency fits even רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: a vessel that broke and was patched back together with pitch

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי אליעזר agrees that you may break a barrel to reach food, if the barrel was already a patched-up broken vessel.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When that was taught,
it was about a barrel patched with pitch.
phrases.notes: It had already broken once and been glued back together, so breaking it now doesn't wreck a whole vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is about a specific kind of barrel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow breaking any whole barrel, which would argue with רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about a barrel that was already broken and patched, so it fits רבי אליעזר too.

steps.title: Gathering kindling from the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about gathering from the courtyard and brings a ברייתא: gathering is allowed, but not into piles. רבי שמעון permits even piles.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one may gather from the courtyard. The Rabbis taught: One may gather from the courtyard and light a fire, because everything in the courtyard counts as prepared. But he may not make piles. רבי שמעון permits even that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that adds a detail and a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things lying in the courtyard are already מוכן, so they are not מוקצה and may be used as fuel. The ברייתא adds a limit: the חכמים forbid gathering them into piles, but רבי שמעון allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: gathers up loose bits like straw or twigs
prepared; ready for use on יום טוב

phrases.english: "And one may gather from the courtyard."
The Rabbis taught:
One may gather from the courtyard and kindle,
for everything in the courtyard is prepared,
provided that he does not make piles and piles.
And Rabbi Shimon permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְגַבֵּב מִן הֶחָצֵר. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gathering from the courtyard for fuel is allowed. The חכמים forbid making piles, and רבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: What is the argument about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lies behind the disagreement between the חכמים and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind each side. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that gathering is allowed. The question is why making piles changes things for the חכמים but not for רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָא מִפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reasoning splits the חכמים and רבי שמעון on making piles?

steps.title: Looks like storing vs. the pot proves it
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים worry it looks like he is storing fuel for after יום טוב. רבי שמעון says his cooking pot shows what the fuel is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: One view holds: it looks like he is gathering for tomorrow and another day. The other view holds: his pot proves what he is doing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both sides. The argument is about how the act looks to people watching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, piles look like stocking up for weekdays, which would mean preparing on יום טוב for another day. רבי שמעון answers that people can see his pot on the fire, so they understand the fuel is for today's cooking.

keyTerms.meaning: proves about him; shows his intent

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים forbid piles because it looks like stocking up for later. רבי שמעון permits them because the pot on the fire shows the fuel is for today.

phrases.english: One master holds:
phrases.notes: This first 'master' is the חכמים, who forbid piles.

phrases.english: It looks like he is gathering
for tomorrow and for another day.
And the other master holds:
His pot proves about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: מִחֲזֵי דְּקָא מְכַנֵּיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים worry about how it looks (stocking up for later days). רבי שמעון says the pot on the fire shows the fuel is for today.

steps.title: Why no new fire on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule against producing fire and asks for its reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one may not bring out fire. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks why this is forbidden. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking on יום טוב is allowed, and so is using an existing fire. So it is not obvious why making a brand-new fire from stones or wood should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: bringing out (producing) fire, as from stones or wood

phrases.english: "One may not bring out fire, etc."
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָאוּר וְכוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is producing new fire forbidden on יום טוב, when cooking is allowed?

steps.title: Because it creates something new
steps.stepSummary: Making fire is forbidden because it brings something new into being on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he is creating something new on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: making a new fire counts as creating something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a fire that already exists is fine. Making a fire that did not exist before counts as creating something new, and that is not allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: creates something new; brings into being

phrases.english: Because he is creating something new on Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מוֹלֵיד בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Producing fire counts as creating something new (מוליד) on יום טוב.

steps.title: What is wrong with heating tiles?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on whitening tiles and asks what forbidden act is involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one may not whiten tiles. What is he doing wrong?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks why heating tiles is forbidden. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heating tiles red-hot to roast food on them seems like ordinary food preparation, which is allowed on יום טוב. So the גמרא asks what makes it different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he doing (that is wrong)?

phrases.english: "And one may not whiten the tiles."
phrases.notes: This is from our משנה. 'Whitening' means heating clay tiles until they glow, so food can be roasted on them.

phrases.english: What is he doing?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מְלַבְּנִין אֶת הָרְעָפִים. מַאי קָא עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What forbidden act happens when someone heats tiles to cook on them?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the case is about new tiles
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the משנה is talking about new tiles. His reason begins here and continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Here we are dealing with new tiles, because...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן begins to answer by saying the case is about brand-new tiles. The reason for the ban continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the tiles are new tells us the problem is not the cooking itself. Heating new tiles does something to the tile, and the reason given next explains what that is.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Here we are dealing with new tiles,
because...

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָכָא בִּרְעָפִים חֲדָשִׁים עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is about new tiles. The reason for the ban continues past the end of this section.
